forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

news_drafts.headline: Colchester reorganisation panel hears of reported £13.2m adult social care overspend at Essex County Council
news_drafts.lead:
A member of Colchester's Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) Transformation and Transition Panel referred to "a reported £13.2 million overspend in adult social care at Essex County Council", according to the panel's draft minutes of 9 September 2026.

The figure came up in discussion of the underlying financial and service pressures facing the area. The minutes describe it as a reported figure for another authority. They do not say how it was sourced, or which year or part of a year it covers.

The £13.2m is Essex County Council's figure, not Colchester's, and the minutes are still in draft.
news_drafts.paper_title: LGR Transformation and Transition Panel draft minutes - 9 September 2026

news_drafts.headline: Colchester's forecast 2026-27 day-to-day deficit falls from £2.4m at quarter 1 to about £1m at quarter 2
news_drafts.lead:
Colchester City Council's General Fund, the account that pays for council services other than housing and schools, is forecast to overspend by about £1 million this year, down from £2.4m forecast at the end of the first quarter. Officers gave the quarter 2 figure as an "emerging" position to the Governance and Audit Committee, whose draft minutes of 8 September 2026 record it.

The quarter 1 forecast was driven by temporary accommodation and homelessness, waste, and the corporate landlord function. Officers told the committee the forecast is a point-in-time assessment and that the position has improved since quarter 1. They also said the quarter 2 figure could prove optimistic. A similar deficit at the same stage of the previous year ended with a small surplus.

The minutes also record a forecast shortfall at Leisure World, which covers the pool, personal training, beauty services and Aqua Springs. The shortfall arose from Leisure World income targets, and investment in the pool is intended to improve future income. Officers said a sinking fund, a pot of money built up over time for a known future cost, might be needed to manage risks including vacant units at the Northern Gateway Leisure Park.
news_drafts.paper_title: Governance and Audit Committee draft minutes - 8 September 2026

news_drafts.headline: Colchester panel cites reported £13.2m adult social care overspend at Essex County Council
news_drafts.lead:
A member of Colchester's Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) Transformation and Transition Panel pointed to a reported £13.2 million overspend in adult social care at Essex County Council, the papers for the Cabinet meeting of 21 October 2026 show. Adult social care is the council service that provides care and support for adults.

The reference appears in the panel's recommendation to Cabinet at item 08(iv). The papers say the panel member highlighted "underlying financial and service pressures in the wider Essex area" and gave the figure as context for continued partnership working.

The overspend is Essex County Council's, not Colchester's. The papers give no period for it and no breakdown of where within adult social care it arose. They do not say what Cabinet is asked to decide in response to it.
news_drafts.paper_title: Item 08(iv) LGR Transformation and Transition Panel recommendation

findings.paper_title: Item 8(ii) - Appendix 1 - Audit Recommendations Tracker Q3
findings.headline: An independent chair is being recruited for Amphora, following approval of new governance arrangements for the company.
findings.detail: The paper says Amphora has commissioned its own experts, including an independent tax expert, and that new board members have had training. It adds that the Council now requires a business case for funding requests from its companies.
findings.matters: Councils with wholly owned companies are comparing how they oversee them after external review, and the paper shows one council's steps.
findings.quote: an independent chair is being recruited

findings.paper_title: Item 8(ii) - Appendix 1 - Audit Recommendations Tracker Q3
findings.headline: KPMG reported an asset value understatement of £26.4m between the initial and revised valuation reports for a single asset, and the 25/26 valuations are recorded as completed.
findings.detail: The paper says the Council's finance team lacked the expertise to challenge the valuation methodology. Management says valuation specialists have been changed, with Montagu Evans LLP for investment properties and NPS Property Consultants Ltd for other valuations, and that audit has reviewed the critical assets.
findings.matters: A valuation understatement of this size on one asset is relevant to other councils and lenders assessing how well their valuation challenge works.

findings.paper_title: Item 8(ii) - Appendix 1 - Audit Recommendations Tracker Q3
findings.headline: Two Northern Gateway infrastructure assets with carrying values totalling £4.8m were transferred out of Assets Under Construction in FY24/25, although practical completion was in October 2021.
findings.detail: KPMG found the assets were given an indefinite 999-year useful life, while the client confirmed a 40-year life was appropriate. The paper says depreciation was understated as a result.
findings.matters: Delayed transfer of completed assets and an incorrect useful life are the kind of error a lender or peer council would check in the accounts.

findings.paper_title: Item 8(ii) - Appendix 1 - Audit Recommendations Tracker Q3
findings.headline: E-Financials version 5.5 is recorded as unsupported with no upgrade option, and Integra has been selected as the replacement finance system.
findings.detail: KPMG reported that the application lacks business ownership and that penetration test responses were suspended for part of the audit period. The Q3 update says a joint options appraisal with North East Essex partners and Essex County Council is scheduled for Cabinet in early September.
findings.matters: Finance system end-of-life and replacement decisions are being made across several councils at once, so peers can compare the options taken.
findings.quote: version 5.5, which is unsupported, end-of-life status, no longer receiving security updates.

findings.paper_title: Item 8(ii) - Appendix 1 - Audit Recommendations Tracker Q3
findings.headline: Integra implementation and budget development are creating "significant capacity pressure" within the Finance team.
findings.detail: The paper says the priority is to deliver a minimum viable product of Integra by February, with further modules in later phases. Concurrent delivery of the new system and budget development is listed as the cause of the pressure.
findings.matters: Other councils moving to new finance systems in the same period face the same pressure on finance staff during budget setting.
